Amazon joins elite list of stocks to top US$3 trillion in value
article:
(Aug 3): Amazon.com Inc surpassed US$3 trillion in market value for the first time, becoming only the fifth company to ever reach the milestone.

The e-commerce and cloud-computing company’s shares rose as much as 5.3% as of 9.35am on Monday, adding to the raucous rally last week following second-quarter earnings that showed accelerating cloud-computing revenue. Amazon joins Nvidia Corp, Alphabet Inc, Microsoft Corp and Apple Inc as the only companies that have reached that size.

Amazon had been mired in a selloff for much of the last three months as investors soured on shares of companies that had committed to spending billions of dollars on artificial intelligence. Its stock sank nearly 18% between its May 6 record and the three-month low it hit last month.

Those fears were eased last week after the firm reported that revenue for its Amazon Web Services unit last quarter jumped by the most since 2021. Shares surged more than 15% in response, their biggest one-day jump in more than 14 years, to add nearly US$400 billion in value.

That’s helped propel Amazon back into position as the best-performing Magnificent Seven stock this year. The gauge of its big tech peers has struggled this year, gaining only 2.1% compared to a 10% gain for the broader S&P 500 Index.

See also: Northrop signs US$3 bil deal to supply missile parts to Lockheed Martin

While the rally has lifted Amazon’s valuation from the 17-year low it hit in late March, it’s still far below where it has traded historically. At roughly 25 times forward earnings for the next 12 months, the stock is about 44% cheaper than its average over the last decade.

It took Amazon just over two years to reach a market capitalisation of US$3 trillion after first hitting US$2 trillion in June 2024. That’s faster than the more than six years between that milestone and when it first hit US$1 trillion in late 2018.

Wall Street remains overwhelmingly upbeat on Amazon’s long-term prospects too. The average analyst price target calls for the stock to rise about 14% over the year from where it currently trades, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

title: Strategy sells more bitcoin, stock as it pushes on with overhaul
article:
(Aug 3): Michael Saylor’s Strategy Inc is ploughing ahead with its pivot from relentlessly buying bitcoin to focusing on shoring up its capital structure by raising its reserve via sales of the token and its own shares.

The company that grew to prominence with its years-long bitcoin-accumulation tactic on Monday announced that it had last week completed a roughly US$105 million sale of the digital asset, offloaded three million shares worth US$291 million and repurchased some US$81 million of of its STRC preferred shares, which are trading at a discount. Some of its common-stock sales went toward increasing its dollar-based reserve pool to US$4 billion while the rest was used to repurchase the preferreds, according to a filing.

At the end of June, Strategy announced an overhaul of its financing model, which had for years underpinned its bitcoin-buying efforts. The shift gave management broader flexibility to sell bitcoin, repurchase securities and preserve liquidity.

Since the announcement was made, Strategy has sold bitcoin and last week said that it had for the first time bought back a portion of the STRC preferred stock, which was designed to trade near or at par. The moves remain small relative to Strategy’s balance sheet but are the latest to help the company adapt to mounting pressure on both bitcoin and the financing model that helped fund its accumulation strategy.

Strategy still holds some US$56 billion in bitcoin, making it the largest corporate holder of the token. Its shares were trading more than 1% lower ahead of Monday’s open. They were down 75% over the past year to around US$93 as of Friday.

title: Northrop signs US$3 bil deal to supply missile parts to Lockheed Martin
article:
(Aug 3): Northrop Grumman Corp has secured agreements worth as much as US$3 billion to supply key components for missile interceptors produced by Lockheed Martin Corp, part of a broader effort to boost output of munitions drawn down by the Iran war.

The framework agreements with the Pentagon cover about US$2 billion in work tied to Lockheed’s Patriot Advanced Capability-3 Missile Segment Enhancement, or PAC-3 MSE, interceptor missile, including the supply of solid rocket motors, said Ben Davies, vice president of defence systems at Northrop.

Northrop also reached a deal worth about US$1 billion to support expanded production of Lockheed’s Terminal High Altitude Area Defence interceptor, or THAAD.

The Trump administration is pushing major defence manufacturers to replenish US munitions stockpiles that have been depleted by years of weapons transfers to Ukraine and heavy use of interceptors during recent operations in the Middle East.

The Pentagon has reached several so-called framework agreements — essentially a formal commitment ahead of a contract award — with Lockheed, Northrop and other weapons makers to boost the effort, which also aims to bolster supplies of key munitions that would be needed in the event of a prolonged conflict with China.

Supplying solid rocket motors for Lockheed’s Patriot missile expands Northrop’s role in the programme, whose sole supplier of the critical system is L3Harris Technologies Inc. Lockheed is working to triple production of the missile to 2,000 a year by the end of 2030.

See also: Chip stocks post biggest advance since April 2025

Northrop expects to ramp up production of the motors over the next two to three years at its facility in West Virginia. The company is in the process of tripling its production capacity there, Davies said. The company said the framework agreement will be followed by a production contract with Lockheed in the coming months.

The company also will continue supplying ignition safety devices for the PAC-3 interceptor.

Northrop’s THAAD agreement expands its existing work supplying high-temperature structural components and supports the Defense Department’s goal of quadrupling production.

See also: Yum reports strong Taco Bell sales in months before parasite-linked outbreak

The new deals follow a broader US$2 billion investment by Northrop in its missile business since 2019. The company has expanded capacity in Utah, West Virginia and Maryland in anticipation of higher demand for missile propulsion systems.

title: India’s new stock closing auction sparks confusion on debut
article:
(Aug 3): India’s new system to discover end-of-day market prices got off to a confusing start, with traders trying to make sense of a spike in the NSE Nifty 50 Index stemming from the shift.

Starting Monday, the National Stock Exchange of India began holding a closing auction session to determine the day’s final prices for stocks with derivatives tied to them. That replaced the volume-weighted average price of trades executed in the final 30 minutes of the session.

The change aims to improve price discovery, curb manipulation and bring India’s market structure closer to that of global peers. Instead, the debut sparked confusion across trading desks, evoking reactions on social media.

“This upmove is essentially fake and will reflect as a gap down tomorrow morning, things remaining unchanged overnight,” said Mayank Bansal, a Dubai-based trader at a hedge fund that trades Indian derivatives.

The Nifty 50 closed 0.8% above the level it was trading at just before the auction began at 3.15pm local time while the BSE Sensex showed little comparable movement. The divergence prompted many market participants to question whether the new mechanism applied only to the NSE.

A spokesperson for the NSE did not immediately respond to a text message seeking comment.

See also: India to push tax bill for global bond funds amid parliament din

“The close is bizarre, perhaps due to the thin volumes in the closing auction, and completely alters all expiry-day dynamics,” Bansal said. “If it continues to stay this far away from the 3.15pm level, one can expect a massive drop in expiry-day volumes.”

title: Dollar drops further as yen rebound extends Fed-driven slide
article:
(Aug 3): The dollar extended its slide on Monday as a joint US-Japan intervention to support the yen added to losses triggered by last week’s Federal Reserve meeting.

Bloomberg’s Dollar Spot Index traded at a one-month low earlier in the day, losing 0.5% against Group-of-10 currencies. It later recouped most of those losses to trade 0.1% lower as of 11:20am in London.

Meanwhile the yen rallied off four-decade lows after the US and Japan took coordinated action to defend it. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has vowed the US “will not hesitate” to wade back into the market, confirming Tokyo has a powerful partner in its bid to stem excessive currency weakness. The greenback was down 0.3% versus the yen.

But its latest bout of weakness can be traced to last week when the Fed opted to keep interest rates on hold, raising question marks over new chairman Kevin Warsh’s inflation-fighting credentials. The dollar index shed 1.3% last week.

“It all started after that Fed meeting,” said Francesco Pesole, an FX strategist at ING. “Markets were quite long the dollar. If you look at positioning gauges, short-term investors were aggressively long dollars across the board.”

See also: Dollar heads for worst week in three months as Fed doubts grow

Bullish dollar wagers were at the highest since 2014 ahead of the July 28-29 Fed meeting, data showed late Friday.

To avoid pressuring the greenback further, the Treasury may have used euros rather than dollars to fund its yen purchases, strategists said. The euro has weakened against most of its Group-of-10 peers since Japan began its recent bout of intervention on July 30.

Many traders will be mulling whether to embrace a structural short position on the dollar, according to Pesole. He says, however, that yen intervention is a temporary fix and the Fed is what will determine the dollar’s trajectory.

See also: Japan declines to confirm yen intervention, hints at US support

Money markets are pricing in an almost 70% chance of an interest-rate increase next month, with a full increase expected by year-end. Jefferies strategist Mohit Kumar said without a sharp oil-price drop, failure to act on inflation will undermine Warsh’s credibility.

“Beyond intervention, I see fundamentals as still negative for the yen and positive for dollar,” Kumar said. “There would be increasing pressure on the Fed to hike.”

title: China LGFV says it can repay debt even as bond sale hits snag
article:
(Aug 3): A Chinese municipal borrower said it has enough funds to repay 1.08 billion yuan in offshore notes due next week, after people familiar with the matter said a plan to refinance that debt with a new bond sale had been delayed.

Luoyang Shangdu City Investment Holding Group Co was scheduled to price a 364-day yuan-denominated offshore bond last Friday to help repay the notes but the deal was postponed due to disagreements with investors over pricing, the people said, asking not to be identified as the matter is private.

The local government financing vehicle said it has ready cash and will repay two yuan offshore bonds — a 6.9% bond and a 7.9% note — both set to mature on Aug 11, on time, responding to queries from Bloomberg News. The company didn’t provide further details and declined comment on whether it will try to sell the offshore bond again this week.

The circumstances surrounding Luoyang Shangdu show the challenges faced by distressed LGFVs in the country despite government support as they try to exhaust all means to meet debt payments.

Thousands of LGFVs have built up massive debt after years of helping China’s towns and cities raise funds for a range of infrastructure projects including roads and public housing. They have about 16 trillion yuan worth of bonds outstanding, with roughly five trillion yuan set to mature by the end of 2027, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

The company, based in China’s central Henan province, showed signs of financial distress after it was placed on a Chinese court list in October following its failure to pay a court enforcement claim of 322,354 yuan, according to its filing to the Shanghai Stock Exchange. It also had 10 million yuan in overdue payments outstanding as of end-April this year, according to a person with knowledge of the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity.

See also: China Mobile said to be to mulling stake sale in Thailand’s True — Bloomberg

It reported 16 million yuan in profit last year on revenue of 250 million yuan, with its liability-to-asset ratio at 67.33%, according to a separate filing to the Shanghai Stock Exchange. Its 6.9% bond was indicated at around 97% of its face value on Friday, according to Bloomberg-compiled data.

LGFVs were once flagged as the top financial risk in Asia but borrowing costs fell to a record low after China told banks and provincial governments to help LGFVs repay domestic and offshore debt maturing no later than June 30, 2027.

However, some weaker LGFVs have been facing refinancing pressure following a slew of measures taken by Chinese regulators, Bloomberg has reported. They’re also discouraged from raising money offshore at higher yields.

title: Former Ping An Group executive joins DBS board
article:
Chinese financial conglomerate Ping An Group’s former chief innovation officer, Jonathan Larsen has joined the board of DBS Group Holdings (SGX:D05 ) and DBS Bank.

Larsen, 60, retired from Ping An Group in February 2026. He joined the company in May 2017 and was also the chairman and CEO of the Ping An Global Voyager Fund.

Prior to joining Ping An, Larsen spent 18 years at Citigroup where held several appointments, including as its global head of retail banking and CEO of Citibank Singapore. Before that, Larsen was a principal at the management consulting firm Booz Allen & Hamilton, where he was a part of the firm’s financial services practice.

“Jonathan brings a unique combination of financial services expertise, technology leadership and innovation experience, shaped through decades of senior leadership at leading global and Asian financial institutions,” DBS chairman Peter Seah says of Larsen. “His perspectives will be highly valuable as the DBS Boards continue to guide the bank through an increasingly dynamic and technology-driven environment.”

title: The post-pandemic travel boom is finally losing steam
article:
(Aug 3): The post-pandemic travel boom is starting to lose steam as high fuel prices, the war in Iran and persistent flying headaches deterred travellers from booking international trips for this year’s peak summer season.

The number of US travellers flying internationally this June fell by 3.2% from the year prior — the first drop for that month in five years — the US International Trade Administration reported. Bookings for trips from the US to Europe this July were down 5.7% from last year and, despite the World Cup, travel from Europe to the US fell 7.9% during the same time period, according to the data analytics firm Cirium.

“As international airfare and other travel costs rise, more Americans are staying at home," said Jan Freitag, the national director of hospitality analytics at CoStar.

Travel from the US to Athens and Rome each fell by more than 10% from a year ago, with many other major hubs seeing drops as well, according to Cirium data.

Summer is usually peak travel season, yet with airfares up 26.5% from a year ago, many people are adjusting plans. Some let points dictate their vacations or choose cheaper “destination dupes". Others decided to stay close to home or sought the comfort of all-inclusive pricing.

See also: The complete package

Global airlines say rising fuel costs are continuing to drag on profits. Though some airlines say demand remains strong, despite rising fares.

Marissa Strang has embraced the “art of the road trip” this summer. After seeing airfares spike, the 29-year-old and her husband decided to drive nine hours from Washington, DC, to Chattanooga, Tennessee, for a four-day getaway. Earlier this year, they went to Egypt but used rewards and points to cut flight costs down to under US$400 (RM1,638.24) round trip for both of them.

American travel to the Middle East saw the most dramatic decline, according to CoStar. Travel to the region dropped by almost 25% in the second quarter from a year earlier while the number of travellers from the Middle East to the US fell by 20%.

See also: Chicago airports cancel hundreds of flights as storms swirl

“The war in Iran clearly had a negative impact on general global propensity to travel but specifically Americans’ desire to go abroad,” said CoStar’s Freitag, adding that he expects US hotels to get a boost instead.

Akylah Cox, who lives in Chicago, took two “microtips” this summer — one or two night visits closer to home. Her guiding question, the 26-year-old said, was, "Where can I go for the cheapest?”

David Manguluti has cut back on flying this year. Instead of a four-hour flight from New York to Chicago, the Macalester College student booked a 17-hour Amtrak trip to save money. He also scrapped visiting DC for a weekend because the costs just wouldn’t be worth it.

“You need to be able to be truthfully honest with yourself to be like, 'Will I have the joy and happiness that I need to feel okay about spending all this money?’” he said.

title: Fosun unit said to be near deal for Apollo-backed Athora Germany — Bloomberg
article:
(Aug 3): Frankfurter Leben, the life insurance consolidator controlled by China’s Fosun International Ltd, is closing in on a deal to buy Athora Holding Ltd’s German unit, people with knowledge of the process said.

 

A sale of the German business of Athora, which is backed by Apollo Global Management Inc, could be announced as soon as this month, some of the people said, asking not to be identified as the process is private.

Talks could still fall apart or other bidders may emerge, and there’s no certainty an agreement will ultimately be reached, the people added. Representatives for Frankfurter Leben and Athora declined to comment.

Athora has been exploring options for the German division including a potential sale, after struggling to grow, Bloomberg News reported in January. The German business manages a closed-book portfolio of traditional life, unit-linked and pension policies for about 140,000 customers. It has €3.5 billion in assets under management and administration and more than 100 staff.

Athora said earlier this year it will move its headquarters to the UK from Bermuda. The announcement came as the firm completed its purchase of Britain’s Pension Insurance Corp, a transaction that almost doubled Athora’s assets under management and administration to €139 billion. Apollo owns about 24.5% of Athora.

Fosun’s Frankfurter Leben manages about 700,000 insurance contracts with an investment portfolio of roughly €13 billion.

Owners of life insurers as well as dealmaking in the sector have come under increased scrutiny by European regulators following the collapse of Italy’s Eurovita in 2023, which was owned by the UK buyout firm Cinven.

See also: AstraZeneca is said to have explored Bristol Myers merger — Bloomberg
